trigger: reading the fixture's own MUTATION COVERAGE comment against the mutation actually run
summary: Fixture header claimed removing TelemetryDark's and-on() guard reddens CH-5-PROM case 1; mutation-run confirmed it reddens case 3.
classification_rationale: quality-engineer ran the mutation and found the header's own claim factually false, not merely awkward - a truth defect in self-documented test evidence.

trigger: a future edit to the commented block that breaks extract_marked_block's shape (indent, marker placement)
summary: --selftest exercised extract_marked_block only against synthetic text, never the real yuzu-alerts.yml block, so a real-file break was caught only by the non-required docs-lint.yml job, not the three required build legs.
classification_rationale: capability gap: a fast no-toolchain regression check was silently absent for this one code path.

trigger: a fork PR commits a symlink at tests/prometheus/generated or the extracted-rules file path
summary: materialize_extracted_rules() wrote through a pre-existing symlink at its destination rather than refusing it; had the umask-077 chmod fix but not the raze-before-write half its sibling build_canary_tree() has.
classification_rationale: truth: the code's own behavior under a planted symlink, not a wording issue.

trigger: two invocations of run_promtool_tests.py against the same checkout, overlapping mid-canary
summary: Fixed-path .promtool-canary/ scratch dir, now used by TWO sequential gate() calls per invocation instead of one, could race under same-checkout concurrent invocation and have an I/O ambiguity misread as a genuine canary redden.
classification_rationale: truth: a race condition in the harness's own evidence-generation logic.

trigger: reading extract_marked_block's actual prefix-matching code against the doc's description of it
summary: New paragraph said extraction 'strips one # comment prefix per line' without noting the two-space indent is load-bearing (a group at another depth fails closed with no warning from this doc).
classification_rationale: doc text was imprecise, not factually contradicting the code's outcome.

trigger: reading gate()'s docstring after its parameterization to serve two (rules,tests,canary) triples
summary: gate()'s docstring and one sys.exit message still said 'the shipped rules' throughout even though the function is now called for the never-shipped extracted group too.
classification_rationale: stale phrasing, not a behavioral contradiction.

trigger: an editor changing the extracted TelemetryDark guard text without knowing it is the canary target
summary: The extracted canary's mutation target (TelemetryDark's and-on() guard) has no in-file CANARY ANCHOR marker the way the shipped canary's target does; the exactly-one-match check still fails closed, so this is convenience only.
classification_rationale: optional polish, no behavioral gap - the exactly-one check already fails closed.

trigger: a duplicated PROMTOOL-EXTRACT marker from a merge-conflict accident
summary: extract_marked_block's 'found N' fail-closed messages omit line numbers (unlike the sibling 'not after' branch), requiring a grep rather than a jump-to-line to debug.
classification_rationale: diagnostic-quality only; the fail-closed path itself is correct and actionable.

trigger: markers relocated to straddle the wrong content without renaming EXTRACT_GROUP
summary: materialize_extracted_rules() validates groups/rules presence but never checks the extracted group's name: matches EXTRACT_GROUP; self-limiting in practice (canary anchor + FIRE assertions catch most drift) but not by explicit design.
classification_rationale: a real but narrow coverage gap in the harness's own self-check.

trigger: a real promtool timeout during a canary leg
summary: run()'s (1, '') timeout sentinel is reported downstream as 'promtool exited 1', misdiagnosing a hang as a clean-but-uninformative exit.
classification_rationale: diagnostic text asserts something not quite true about what happened (a real timeout reads as a real exit code).

trigger: docker image pruned/evicted on a shared box between gate 1 and gate 2 of one invocation
summary: pull_with_retry() runs once before both gates; an implicit re-pull triggered by gate 2 is not covered by its retry ladder. Confirmed N/A for actual CI (docs-lint.yml is GHA-hosted, fresh checkout per job, no shared box).
classification_rationale: theoretical operational gap, explicitly scoped out of the real CI environment by UP-9.

trigger: an extraction failure on the (production-inert) commented block
summary: materialize_extracted_rules() runs before gate 1, so a hygiene failure in the never-shipped extracted block masks whether the shipped rules passed. Gate-6 sre confirmed the FAIL message does correctly name the cause, so this is diagnostic ordering, not misdiagnosis.
classification_rationale: control-flow ordering observation, no false result.

trigger: any sys.exit FAIL site failing inside GitHub Actions
summary: None of the sys.exit FAIL sites (several new in this PR) call gh_error(), so a red job shows no ::error:: annotation in the GH Checks summary. Pre-existing pattern, surface roughly doubled by new FAIL sites.

trigger: a promtool syntax/semantic error in the extracted block during CI
summary: Gate-2 promtool errors cite line numbers in the gitignored generated file (invisible in the CI log, and offset from yuzu-alerts.yml's real line numbers) - a CI-only failure needs a local repro to read the offending line.
classification_rationale: diagnostic-quality gap in a new code path.

trigger: a hypothetical third gate() caller passing mismatched positional/keyword file pairs
summary: gate()'s rules_rel/tests_rel/canary_from/canary_to default to the shipped-file constants; nothing enforces pairing with the positional rules/tests args passed by a future third caller. Confirmed fails closed today via the canary's own rule-count guard.
classification_rationale: forward-looking maintainability note, no live defect; architect's own recommendation is to defer to the PR that adds a third group.

trigger: a third not-yet-enabled alert group needing the same extraction treatment
summary: gate() is hand-duplicated at 4 call sites (native/docker x shipped/extracted) rather than looped over a list of triples; acceptable for a 2-group case, architect recommends the refactor land with a third group.
classification_rationale: maintainability observation, no operational impact today.

trigger: a hard-kill (SIGKILL/OOM/CI timeout) while a canary tree exists under REPO_ROOT
summary: Found in Gate 8 re-review of the f04 fix: the new per-call mkdtemp naming has no pre-emptive sweep the old fixed-path version got for free, so a killed run's uniquely-named orphan is never revisited. Disk clutter only - both fixtures' rule_files globs point elsewhere, so an orphan can never be loaded by a later run; CI legs unaffected (checkout is clean per job).
classification_rationale: genuine but narrow resource-hygiene note on the f04 fix itself.
